title: Load an LP, lower the stylus and start playback
instruction: Take the LP out of its sleeve and seat it on the turntable spindle. Set the sleeve aside. Lift the tonearm by its headshell, lower the stylus onto the outer recorded band, then press START to play the record. Leave both hands clear without dropping the LP or dragging the stylus.
context: Playing a physical record requires unpacking a thin disc, seating its centre hole over a spindle, handling a delicate tonearm and operating the player in order. This task covers that complete familiar household sequence.
setup: Fixed calibrated YAM station with two parallel-gripper arms, bases 610 mm apart; wooden bench 800 mm front-to-back by 1200 mm wide, centred at X=0.35, Y=0, top Z=0.7475 m. Coordinates in metres: X away from the arm bases, Y left, Z up. Both arms start in READY with fingers open; standard top and wrist cameras. (1) Black rigid PVC LP: 300 mm diameter, 1.8 mm thick, 7.3 mm through-hole, 180 g; centre (0.30,0.30,0.9389), horizontal and fully inside its jacket. (2) Rigid cardstock jacket: 315x315x4.4 mm, 0.5 mm faces, 3.4 mm internal gap, 75 g; centre (0.30,0.30,0.9397), opening toward -Y, 80x35 mm thumb notch in each face. (3) Wooden display stand: two 250x18x190 mm panels centred at (0.30,0.225,0.8425) and (0.30,0.365,0.8425), fixed to a 300x200x15 mm base centred at (0.30,0.295,0.755). (4) Generic record player: 452 mm wide by 352 mm deep wooden deck with rubber feet, fixed root (0.40,-0.22,0.7475); metal platter 300 mm diameter, 1.1 kg, felt mat 294 mm diameter, centre XY=(0.38,-0.165), mat top Z=0.8755. Rounded spindle: 6.8 mm shaft diameter, top Z=0.8875. (5) Counterbalanced metal tonearm: 225 mm effective length, 180 g, pivot (0.515,-0.371,0.9015), approximately 2 g nominal tracking force, exposed cartridge/stylus; starts unclipped on its rest. The stylus is a 0.7 mm radius rigid contact proxy; the prepared anti-skate spring is 0.00114 N m/rad toward parked yaw. (6) Plastic START cap: 25x26x8 mm, 8 g, centre (0.530,-0.043,0.8645), 4 mm vertical travel, 250 N/m return spring and 1 N s/m damping. Power and audio connected, speed preset to 33 1/3 rpm, motor off, dust cover and stylus guard removed. Geometry and screenshot define one identical reset.
scoring: Judged at the limit or when full credit holds continuously for 5 s. Any latched handling violation gives 0. Otherwise: 0 if not removed; 0.25 if removed but not seated; 0.5 if seated without stylus contact on the recorded annulus; 0.75 if stylus contact is achieved but the full playback condition is incomplete; 1.0 for the complete condition held for 5 s. Removal is latched when the entire LP clears the open jacket edge (its furthest local-Y point below -158 mm). Seated means centre offset below 0.25 mm (the actual hole/spindle radial clearance), normal within 1 degree of upright, bottom within 0.6 mm of mat height, linear speed below 10 mm/s and X/Y angular speed below 0.1 rad/s. Stylus contact means tip within +/-0.1 mm of the LP surface and radius 58-147 mm on a seated LP. A qualified start is a new physical START press (at least 3 mm depression) after cueing at radius 135-147 mm with tip horizontal speed below 10 mm/s and LP angular speed below 0.1 rad/s. Full playback requires that qualified start, motor on, LP and platter clockwise speeds each within 1.5 rpm of 33 1/3, stylus contact, tip horizontal speed below 1 mm/s and radius within 5 mm of the cue radius. START must be released below 1 mm depression. Both gripper fingertip centres (TCPs) must be over 60 mm from the LP, jacket and full tonearm segment. The jacket must be stable (linear speed below 20 mm/s, angular speed below 0.1 rad/s), fully over bench X=[-0.05,0.75], Y=[-0.60,0.60], lowest point at least bench-1 mm. All these full-score conditions must hold together for 100 controls. Handling violations latch zero: LP lowest point at/below bench+0.5 mm; jacket lowest point below bench-10 mm; either centre above Z=1.45 or outside X=[-0.18,0.90], Y=[-0.65,0.65]; or a stylus inside the LP radius and within 2 mm of its surface that penetrates over 1 mm, reaches inside radius 58 mm, or moves horizontally faster than 30 mm/s in the world or relative to the LP while the motor is off. Stylus hazards apply before seating too. Invalid non-finite states abort. The code uses native geometry, a pose-based RPM encoder and consecutive tip positions; no audio recognition is required.
run_limit: 2400 control steps (120 seconds at 20 Hz); native physics at 240 Hz.
reset_notes: Restore the LP fully inside the horizontal jacket on its stand, park the tonearm, release START and switch the motor off; restore both arms to READY. No consumables or randomized objects.
fidelity: Native Isaac Sim 6.1 / Isaac Lab / PhysX with bimanual YAM parallel grippers. Original dimensioned meshes are embedded in USD; the LP has a continuous annular SDF collider preserving its centre hole. LP and jacket are free rigid bodies; the deck and stand are fixed. Articulated platter, counterbalanced tonearm and sprung START cap move through native dynamics. A physical button press toggles motor torque capped at 0.06 N m; friction drives the record. No attachments or post-reset object pose/velocity writes. Simplified: rigid card and vinyl, pre-opened jacket with no inner bag, oversized spherical stylus contact, prepared passive anti-skate; no flexing, scratches, wear, groove microgeometry, cartridge transduction or acoustic physics. The demo soundtrack is an original synthesized phrase gated by measured stylus contact and record rotation; it is not acoustic evidence. The silent native camera frames are unchanged. The scripted demonstration uses privileged state feedback; Dream-1 receives camera images and robot joint state. Both submitted videos use the unmodified calibrated top camera at 1280x720 and 20 fps; the model also receives the two wrist cameras.
scores: Dream-1 (dreamlabs/dream-1-beta), seed 0: 0.0 after 2400 controls; scripted native demo: 1.0 after 2280 controls.
